insights.title: Youth pathways are the cleanest first wedge
insights.summary: Schools, career training, higher education, health anchors, and employers are close enough to model as one relationship system.
insights.recommendation: Use the first buyer conversation around youth opportunity and workforce pathway friction, then show how AVRAI detects missing links.
insights.buyerSignal: Workforce councils, chambers, hospitals, schools, and funders all have incentive to reduce this coordination cost.

insights.title: Healthcare access is a relationship problem, not only a facility problem
insights.summary: The graph shows major medical assets, but the valuable layer is the trusted routing between clinics, behavioral health, churches, schools, and families.
insights.recommendation: Frame the health demo around governed social-need routing, not a generic provider directory.
insights.buyerSignal: Hospitals and care coalitions can justify spend if the graph improves referral completion, navigation, or community benefit reporting.

insights.title: Downtown vitality can be sold as coordination leverage
insights.summary: Downtown has civic, faith, library, and merchant nodes close together. The missing product is a live view of which event, support, or referral action helps the corridor.
insights.recommendation: Show one story where a library event, merchant need, and trusted community node become one coordinated intervention.
insights.buyerSignal: Main street groups, chambers, city economic development teams, and local funders can understand this quickly.

insights.title: The integrity layer is the business-model filter
insights.summary: The graph becomes monetizable when buyers see that AVRAI can hold live city data without becoming surveillance or extractive adtech.
insights.recommendation: Use data lineage, confidence, synthetic users, and permission boundaries as visible product features in the demo.
insights.buyerSignal: Values-aligned buyers need evidence and shared context, but they also need defensible boundaries around community data.

insights.title: Westgate is an easy visual story for access friction
insights.summary: Schools, the library branch, grocery, retail, and hospital-side assets cluster together, but the graph can expose timing and transport gaps.
insights.recommendation: Use Westgate as the guided story for showing how AVRAI sees coordination gaps that a map alone misses.
insights.buyerSignal: A local funder or family-services coalition can sponsor a narrow pilot around program matching and access friction.

insights.title: Dothan works best as a regional hub story
insights.summary: The strongest place graph is Dothan plus the Wiregrass catchment, because hospitals, colleges, libraries, and referral actors serve beyond city limits.
insights.recommendation: Call the prototype Dothan / Wiregrass rather than only Dothan city limits.
insights.buyerSignal: Regional institutions can buy a system that makes their real catchment legible.

storySteps.title: Dothan is the right scale
storySteps.body: The prototype treats Dothan as a human-scale regional hub: compact enough to see the whole system, complex enough to reveal civic, health, school, business, and rural-edge relationships.
storySteps.question: Who needs a shared view of this place badly enough to pay for it?

storySteps.title: Assets are already present
storySteps.body: The map is not saying Dothan lacks assets. It shows schools, libraries, hospitals, colleges, parks, faith anchors, and business nodes already exist inside a dense relationship layer.
storySteps.question: Which relationships are missing, stale, or invisible?

storySteps.title: Youth opportunity is the wedge
storySteps.body: A workforce story connects high school, technical education, community college, medical education, employers, mentors, transportation, and after-school timing.
storySteps.question: Where would one new relationship unlock the most next action?

storySteps.title: Health is routing plus trust
storySteps.body: The health story becomes compelling when AVRAI shows not only providers, but the trusted handoffs among care teams, schools, churches, rural referrals, and family support organizations.
storySteps.question: Which buyer would pay to reduce failed handoffs?

storySteps.title: Westgate shows map-plus-graph value
storySteps.body: On a map, Westgate looks asset-rich. In the graph, the question shifts to program hours, rides, trust, and whether the right actors know they are near the same problem.
storySteps.question: What does the graph reveal that a normal dashboard would miss?

storySteps.title: Integrity filters the business model
storySteps.body: The prototype makes lineage, confidence, and synthetic personas visible so the whiteboard can focus on values-aligned buyers instead of extractive data monetization.
storySteps.question: Who values trusted shared context enough to fund the live layer?
